subject.title: Feature Request: Image batching / media group buffering at gateway layer

question: Should the remaining rapid-media batching behavior be accepted as a LINE-owned opt-in config surface, designed as a broader shared channel/plugin contract, or intentionally left unsupported for channels without native grouping metadata?
rationale: The remaining request adds delayed webhook behavior and a new config surface for a channel without native grouping metadata, so automation should not choose the product boundary, default, or heuristic semantics on its own.

options.title: LINE opt-in batching
options.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key and buffer same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media while documenting latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

options.title: Shared channel contract
options.body: Design a media-aware channel SDK/core contract first, accepting broader architecture and compatibility review before changing LINE.

options.title: Keep unsupported
options.body: Keep Telegram's native media-group handling only and document that channels without reliable grouping metadata dispatch media events individually.

recommendation.title: LINE opt-in batching
recommendation.body: Add a conservative LINE plugin config key and buffer same-account, same-conversation, same-sender downloadable media while documenting latency and reply-token tradeoffs.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses LINE config, shared channel semantics, and plugin-boundary policy where history shows repeated recent ownership.
